before.requirement: Built-in PRIORITY_UPDATE reception and local SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1.
before.reason: The before receiver has no built-in PRIORITY_UPDATE case; an unknown extension is ignored. The new receive behavior therefore has no before-side counterpart.

after.requirement: Enable built-in PRIORITY_UPDATE reception and submit local SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 before receiving a valid PRIORITY_UPDATE frame.
after.reason: The target passes no option, leaving the built-in receive mask unset, and submits only MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS. The new receiver ignores PRIORITY_UPDATE at the mask check; even with that mask enabled, its pending-priority-setting check would ignore the payload.

claims.reason: Built-in PRIORITY_UPDATE handling did not exist before the change. The after-side setup is blocked by the fixed constructor and setting submission.

before.requirement: Submit local SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 so request Priority fields reach the existing extended-priority header path.
before.reason: The before Priority header path already requires a stream marked NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES. The target omits the local setting, so settings submission makes the pending value zero and newly opened streams lack that flag.

after.requirement: Submit local SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 so received request Priority fields exercise the changed valid and bad priority state handling and subsequent priority application.
after.reason: The changed handling retains the stream-flag guard. The same omitted local setting leaves the pending value zero and prevents newly opened streams from receiving that flag.

claims.reason: The concrete blocker is the same on both sides: the fixed harness never submits local SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1. The guarded Priority header path existed before, while its valid/bad state behavior changed after.
